meanings.en: to call for, to summon (a taxi, driver, police, doctor)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to summon', paired with 'вызывать'.

examples.text: Ты же не помнишь ничего. Ты вызвал трезвого водителя!
examples.trans: You don't remember anything, after all. You called a sober driver!

meanings.note: Location; for direction use 'куда'. Core Russian adv meaning 'where' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: В гости = for a visit. Abstract feminine noun formed with the Slavic suffix '-ость' ('-ness, -ity') from the corresponding adjective. Common masculine noun meaning 'guest, visitor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Клавдия Викторовна, к вам гости! Па-пам!
examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, you have visitors! Ta-da!

meanings.note: usually the short form: я готов (m), я готова (f)

Location; compare домой = homeward. Core Russian adv meaning 'at home' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А Осипенко сейчас дома лежит. У него больное сердце.
examples.trans: And Osipenko is lying at home right now. He has a sick heart.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

A door, a shop, or a legal case. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крыть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to close, to shut', paired with 'закрывать'.

examples.text: А потом, Аркадий Борисович, мы закроем ваше дело.
examples.trans: And then, Arkady Borisovich, we will close your case.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'ride, ski'.

examples.text: Пока, ребята, я улетаю в Сочи кататься на лыжах!
examples.trans: Bye, guys, I am flying to Sochi to go skiing!

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и кататься вовремя.

оказываться.gloss: to turn out to be, prove to be

meanings.en: to turn out to be, prove to be, find oneself
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to turn out to be, prove to be', paired with 'оказаться'.

examples.trans: Simple things turn out to be important.

examples.text: Иногда простые вещи оказываются самыми важными.
examples.trans: Sometimes simple things turn out to be the most important.

meanings.note: Что у кого. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'обрать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to take away (by force), confiscate', paired with 'отбирать'.

examples.trans: Oh sure, right now they'll take them away!

examples.trans: Klavdia Viktorovna, listen. If you meddle in what's not your business, we'll take the TVs away!

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'дача'). Common feminine noun meaning 'broadcast, TV show' in everyday Russian.

Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see each other, meet up', paired with 'видеться'.

examples.text: Послушай, мы сегодня увидимся вечером с тобой?
